outputs.L1: In driving a display element that includes an n-channel drive transistor having a drive voltage applied to one source/drain region and a light-emitting unit connected to the other source/drain region, as well as a capacitor connected between a gate electrode and the other source/drain region, processing is performed to: apply the drive voltage to the one source/drain region while a reference voltage is applied to the gate electrode of the drive transistor, thereby bringing a potential of the other source/drain region closer to a potential obtained by subtracting a threshold voltage of the drive transistor from the reference voltage; and subsequently, place the gate electrode in a floating state, change a potential of the gate electrode in the floating state via parasitic capacitance, cause a current to flow through the drive transistor to increase a voltage between the other source/drain region and the gate electrode, and thereafter apply the reference voltage to the gate electrode.
outputs.L2: A display element is driven using an n-channel driving transistor, with a voltage supplied to one of its source/drain regions, a light-emitting unit coupled to the other source/drain region, and a capacitor connected between the gate electrode and that other source/drain region. The driving method includes the following operations: while a reference voltage is supplied to the gate electrode of the driving transistor, a drive voltage is applied to the one source/drain region so that the potential of the other source/drain region approaches a level equal to the reference voltage minus the threshold voltage of the driving transistor. After that, the gate electrode is placed in a floating condition, its potential is varied through parasitic capacitance, and current is made to pass through the driving transistor, thereby increasing the voltage between the other source/drain region and the gate electrode. The reference voltage is then supplied again to the gate electrode.

The display element includes an n-channel drive transistor, a light-emitting unit, and a capacitor. The light-emitting unit is connected to one source/drain region of the drive transistor, while the capacitor is connected between the gate electrode of the drive transistor and that same source/drain region.

In operation, a drive voltage is applied to one source/drain region of the drive transistor, and a reference voltage is applied to the gate electrode. As a result, the potential of the other source/drain region is shifted toward a value corresponding to the reference voltage minus the threshold voltage of the drive transistor. In other words, the potential of this source/drain region is adjusted so as to approach a level determined by subtracting the transistor threshold voltage from the applied reference voltage.

After this potential adjustment, the gate electrode is placed in a floating state. While the gate electrode is floating, its potential is varied through the effect of parasitic capacitance. A current is then made to flow through the drive transistor, thereby increasing the voltage between the other source/drain region and the gate electrode. Subsequently, the reference voltage is applied again to the gate electrode.

Through this sequence of operations, the display element can control the voltage relationship between the gate electrode and the source/drain region of the n-channel drive transistor, thereby enabling appropriate current control for driving the light-emitting unit.

A display driving method is provided for a display element that includes a light-emitting unit, an n-channel drive transistor, and a capacitor connected between the gate of the drive transistor and one of its source/drain regions. The method controls the potential of the gate and the connected source/drain region in a predetermined sequence so that the current supplied through the drive transistor to the light-emitting unit can be accurately set.

In this method, a reference voltage is first applied to the gate of the n-channel drive transistor. The potential of the source/drain region connected to the capacitor is then adjusted in relation to the threshold voltage of the drive transistor. This operation allows the circuit to compensate for variations in the threshold voltage of the drive transistor, which may occur due to manufacturing differences, aging, or temperature changes.

After this threshold-related adjustment, the gate of the drive transistor is placed in a floating state. While the gate is floating, a change in potential at the connected source/drain region is transferred to the gate through parasitic capacitance associated with the drive transistor. As a result, the gate potential is shifted by capacitive coupling. This parasitic-capacitance-induced change increases the voltage between the connected source/drain region and the gate before the reference voltage is applied again.

By increasing this voltage difference in advance, the subsequent reapplication of the reference voltage can be performed under improved electrical conditions. The drive transistor can therefore be more reliably brought into a desired operating state, and the current flowing through the drive transistor can be controlled with greater precision. Since the amount of current supplied to the light-emitting unit determines the luminance of the display element, the method contributes to more stable light emission and improved display quality.

This driving sequence is particularly useful in active-matrix display devices using current-driven light-emitting elements, such as organic electroluminescent elements or other light-emitting diodes. By combining reference-voltage application, threshold-voltage-related potential adjustment, gate floating, and capacitive coupling through parasitic capacitance, the method reduces the influence of transistor characteristic variations and enables stable operation of the display element.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for an invention involving an n-channel drive transistor, a light-emitting element, a storage capacitor, threshold-voltage compensation, and floating-gate operation.
counterfactuals.output: An electronic pixel circuit includes an n-channel drive transistor coupled to a light-emitting element, a storage capacitor configured to store a data-dependent voltage, and compensation circuitry configured to compensate for a threshold voltage of the n-channel drive transistor. During a programming period, a gate node of the drive transistor is set according to image data while the threshold voltage of the drive transistor is sensed or written into the storage capacitor. During an emission period, the gate of the drive transistor is placed in a floating state such that the stored voltage maintains a compensated gate-to-source voltage, causing the drive transistor to supply a drive current to the light-emitting element substantially independent of threshold-voltage variation. The circuit thereby improves luminance uniformity and stability while enabling efficient operation of an active-matrix light-emitting display.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical summary of a method for driving a display element where the source/drain potential is brought near Vref − Vth and the gate potential is later changed in a floating state to adjust current through the drive transistor.
counterfactuals.output:
A display driving method is used to compensate for threshold voltage variation of a drive transistor in a pixel circuit, such as an OLED or current-driven display element pixel.

In the method, a reference potential \(V_{\text{ref}}\) is applied to the gate of the drive transistor while one of the source/drain terminals is charged or discharged so that its potential approaches:

\[
V_{\text{ref}} - V_{\text{th}}
\]

where \(V_{\text{th}}\) is the threshold voltage of the drive transistor. This operation stores information corresponding to the transistor threshold voltage in the pixel, typically on a storage capacitor connected to the gate or source node.

After this threshold-voltage setting or compensation phase, the gate electrode of the drive transistor is placed in a floating state. While floating, the gate potential is subsequently shifted, for example by capacitive coupling from a data signal or control signal. Because the gate node is electrically floating, the applied signal changes the gate potential without directly overwriting the stored threshold-compensation voltage.

As a result, the effective gate-source voltage of the drive transistor is adjusted according to display data while retaining compensation for \(V_{\text{th}}\). The drive current supplied through the drive transistor to the display element is therefore controlled more accurately and is less dependent on transistor threshold variation, mobility variation, or aging effects.

In summary, the method includes:

1. Setting the gate of the drive transistor to a reference voltage \(V_{\text{ref}}\).
2. Bringing a source/drain terminal potential close to \(V_{\text{ref}} - V_{\text{th}}\), thereby reflecting the transistor threshold voltage.
3. Floating the gate node after the compensation operation.
4. Changing the floating gate potential through capacitive coupling or a data-writing operation.
5. Driving the display element with a current determined by the adjusted gate-source voltage of the drive transistor.

This technique enables stable grayscale control and improved uniformity in active-matrix display panels by compensating drive transistor threshold variations before the emission period.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in patent terminology, a compensation sequence for an OLED pixel circuit having an n-channel TFT, a capacitor between gate and output node, and a light-emitting unit connected to the output node.
counterfactuals.output:
In one embodiment, a compensation sequence for an organic light-emitting diode (OLED) pixel circuit is provided. The pixel circuit comprises an n-channel thin film transistor (TFT) having a gate electrode, a first current-carrying electrode, and a second current-carrying electrode; a storage capacitor coupled between the gate electrode of the n-channel TFT and an output node; and a light-emitting unit coupled to the output node.

The compensation sequence may include a reset period, a threshold-voltage sensing or programming period, and an emission period.

During the reset period, the gate electrode of the n-channel TFT and/or the output node is initialized to a predetermined reference voltage. The initialization discharges or precharges the storage capacitor such that a known voltage condition is established across the capacitor. In some embodiments, the light-emitting unit is reverse-biased or otherwise inhibited from emitting light during the reset period.

During the threshold-voltage compensation period, a data voltage or reference voltage is applied to the gate electrode of the n-channel TFT while the output node is allowed to change in response to conduction of the n-channel TFT. Because the storage capacitor is connected between the gate electrode and the output node, the voltage developed across the storage capacitor includes information corresponding to a threshold voltage of the n-channel TFT. The output node may be charged or discharged until the gate-to-source voltage of the n-channel TFT approaches the threshold voltage thereof, thereby storing a compensation voltage on the storage capacitor.

Thereafter, during the data programming period, an image data voltage is written to the pixel circuit. The stored threshold-related voltage is combined with the data voltage by capacitive coupling such that a compensated gate-to-output-node voltage is established for the n-channel TFT. Accordingly, variations in the threshold voltage of the n-channel TFT are at least partially cancelled.

During the emission period, the n-channel TFT supplies a drive current to the light-emitting unit through the output node. The drive current is determined substantially by the programmed data voltage and the compensated voltage stored on the storage capacitor, and is less dependent on threshold-voltage variation of the n-channel TFT. As a result, the light-emitting unit emits light with improved luminance uniformity.
